questions.question: In a classroom model of natural selection, students try to pick up green and white cocktail sticks from a green lawn. What does this simple model demonstrate?
options: How green sticks reproduce faster than white sticks.
How camouflage affects the survival rate of individuals due to predation.
How plants absorb nutrients from different types of soil.
How human activities cause the extinction of various grass species.

questions.question: Using the cocktail stick model on a green lawn, if predators (students) repeatedly feed on the most visible sticks, what prediction can be made about the population over time?
options: The proportion of green sticks in the population will decrease.
The proportion of white sticks in the population will increase.
The proportion of green sticks in the population will increase.
All sticks will eventually turn blue due to environmental pressure.

questions.question: In the cocktail stick model, how would the prediction change if the green lawn became covered in a heavy layer of white frost or snow?
options: Green sticks would now be harder to see and more likely to survive.
White sticks would now have a survival advantage as they blend in with the snow.
Both green and white sticks would become equally easy for predators to find.
The predators would stop eating sticks altogether because of the temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes why polar bears have thick fur and a layer of blubber?
options: They are features that make them well suited to survive in their freezing environment.
They are features they chose to grow to help them swim faster in warm water.
They are features caused by a disease common in cold geographic regions.
They are features designed to help them escape from larger forest predators.

questions.question: What scientific term is used to describe the biological features that make an organism well suited to survive and reproduce in its environment?
options: Variations
Habitats
Adaptations
Classifications

questions.question: Why must all living organisms obtain resources such as food, water, and shelter from their habitat?
options: To enable them to survive and successfully reproduce.
To change the climate of their local ecosystem.
To prevent other species from ever entering their habitat.
To make sure they can undergo artificial selection.

questions.question: Why are individual organisms of the same or different species in constant competition with one another?
options: Because resources in a habitat are limited.
Because organisms naturally prefer to fight than to cooperate.
Because their genes force them to destroy their environment.
Because there is an infinite supply of food and space for everyone.

questions.question: What can happen to the common characteristics of a species over many generations as a result of natural selection?
options: They will remain exactly the same forever, regardless of environmental changes.
They can change over generations, a process known as evolution.
They will instantly change within a single individual's lifetime.
They will become less suited to the environment until the species dies out.

questions.question: In science, what is a "scientific theory", such as the theory of evolution by natural selection?
options: An uneducated guess that has not yet been tested by any scientists.
A general explanation, developed from evidence, that explains many different examples.
A set of rigid rules that cannot be changed even if new evidence is found.
An individual opinion held by a single scientist without any supporting data.

questions.question: How do new advantageous features first appear in a population during the process of evolution?
options: They are planned in advance by the organisms to solve a specific future problem.
They appear randomly and are then maintained over generations by natural selection.
They are actively trained and developed by parents to pass on to their offspring.
They are given to the organisms by other species in the same habitat.

questions.question: An athlete works out regularly and develops very large, strong muscles during their lifetime. Why is this change not considered evolution?
options: Because muscles are not physical features of an organism.
Because changes in the features of an individual within its lifetime are not evolution.
Because the athlete did not train hard enough to alter their species' characteristics.
Because evolution only happens to plants and microorganisms, not humans.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most accurate definition of a fossil?
options: Any ancient bone that has remained completely unchanged and organic since death.
The mineralised remains of once-living organisms or of traces left behind by them.
A drawing made by early humans on cave walls representing ancient animals.
A modern rock that has been carved by wind and rain to look like a plant leaf.

questions.question: A tree loses one of its branches during a severe storm. Why will the offspring grown from its seeds not be missing this branch?
options: Because environmental variation is not heritable and cannot be passed on.
Because the tree will repair its genetic code before producing seeds.
Because only positive changes can be passed on to offspring.
Because seeds are unaffected by any type of variation.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of genetic variation that can be passed on to offspring?
options: A scar on a dog's leg from an old injury.
The ability of a human to speak a second language.
The inherited instructions for making camouflaged skin in lizards.
The increased muscle mass a horse gains from daily training.

questions.question: In the context of natural selection, what does it mean when we say certain individuals are "the fittest"?
options: They can run the fastest and jump the highest compared to all other animals.
They are the individuals that are better adapted to their environment and thus more likely to survive to reproduce.
They have spent the most time exercising and building up their physical strength.
They are the largest and most aggressive individuals in the population.

questions.question: According to scientific evidence, approximately how long ago was the Earth formed?
options: 4.5 million years ago
450 thousand years ago
4.5 billion years ago
3.8 billion years ago

questions.question: Based on scientific evidence, when did the first living organisms (microorganisms) appear on Earth?
options: Around 4.5 billion years ago
Around 3.8 billion years ago
Around 500 million years ago
Around 200 million years ago
